current_goal: Bootstrap kit for a fresh Linux/WSL machine: clone, run install.sh, done.

tasks.title: Normalize keybind mnemonics across zellij/nvim/inner tools
tasks.notes: Semantic consistency of the mnemonic letter, not just collision-avoidance: a given letter should mean the same verb everywhere (e.g. m=move in zellij, not 'mark' elsewhere). Goal: lower cognitive load. Follow-up from the zellij quick-terminal/mode-alignment branch. Collision checker exists (scripts/check-keybind-collisions.py); this is about meaning, not overlap. Also revisit nvim-vs-zellij/ghostty collisions (nvim maps only apply in-pane; zellij globals shadow them).

tasks.title: Install lazygit + wire into nvim and broot
tasks.notes: Researched 2026-07-23. Two consumers: (1) nvim plugin — value narrowed to interactive rebase, partial staging, history browse/cherry-pick; everything else covered by alt+f/delegation. (2) broot: conf.hjson already defines a Ctrl-g verb ('lazygit --path {directory}') that errors harmlessly until lazygit is installed. Shared prereq: add install_lazygit to CLI-extras (packaged on zypper; Ubuntu needs a release binary/PPA). LIGHT scope. Deferred for now. See references.

tasks.title: Consider telescope-fzf-native for faster fuzzy sorting
tasks.notes: C-compiled sorter (needs 'make' at build time); enables fzf syntax ('exact, ^prefix, suffix$). Nice-to-have speed boost over default Lua sorter; evaluate if telescope filtering feels slow.

tasks.title: Document GUI/desktop tools wanted on every new machine
tasks.notes:
Gap between 'configs symlinked' and 'machine actually ready'. Start as docs/tools.md (tool, why, install command per package manager) rather than install.sh logic — package names differ across zypper/apt/pacman, flatpak-vs-native is a per-machine call, and install.sh assuming a package manager cuts against the minimal-dependencies principle. Promote into the installer later if the list stabilizes. Scope now covers CLI tools too, so suggest two sections: the CLI half is natively packaged and scriptable and could plausibly move into install.sh, while GUI stays a per-machine judgment call. GUI settled on DBeaver (flatpak) and resolved the S3 GUI slot as 'no GUI needed'. CLI half (aws-vault, rclone, duckdb) is installed and working as of 2026-07-28, with per-tool install and credential-isolation gotchas in the brief.

See: output/claude-toolkit/backlog-notes/new-machine-tools.md

tasks.title: Split bootstrap into private repo depending on public dotfiles
tasks.notes: Two repos along a privacy line, dependency points one way only: PUBLIC dotfiles (configs, symlinks, install.sh - self-contained, useful to a stranger, never learns bootstrap exists) <- PRIVATE bootstrap (clones dotfiles, runs ./install.sh, then packages + private repos + per-repo setup). Keeps dotfiles genuinely publishable rather than publishable-with-holes, and confines the non-idempotent cloning/setup mess to the private repo so install.sh keeps its symlink-only idempotency. Confirmed as the right home for machine-provisioning concerns (incl. gaming) by the 2026-08-05 Nitro build, and for agent CLI tooling (herdr + pi) on 2026-08-07 - pi is npm-global and would break install.sh's minimal-dependency rule. Install commands and setup gotchas for both are in the brief.

tasks.title: Set up Bitwarden CLI for personal credentials
tasks.notes: Bitwarden is already the password manager in use on Windows and phone; this is about getting it usable from the Linux CLI. Open decision: official 'bw' (Node, npm install -g @bitwarden/cli or native binary from releases - check 'zypper se bitwarden', likely not in openSUSE repos) vs 'rbw' (unofficial Rust client, much faster, has an unlock agent so you are not re-entering the master password constantly; third-party client for the password vault, which is its own trust call). Official bw is required for anything touching org/admin operations. Session handling is the main friction: bw needs BW_SESSION exported and it expires - do NOT put it in .bashrc, it is a live vault-unlock token. Distinct from aws-vault, which stays as-is for AWS only.

tasks.title: Explore Bitwarden CLI for programmatic secret retrieval
tasks.notes: Direction, not a settled plan: use the Bitwarden CLI as a general secret-retrieval layer in scripts instead of scattering tokens across dotfiles and .env files. Shape is 'bw get password NAME' / 'bw get item NAME | jq' inline at the point of use. Depends on bitwarden-cli-setup landing first (client choice + session/agent handling). Two habits worth establishing up front: never persist BW_SESSION in shell init, and prefer passing secrets inline to the single command that needs them over 'export TOKEN=$(bw get ...)', which exposes them to every child process - same reasoning as 'aws-vault exec'. Bitwarden could also be the source of truth for the AWS key (it syncs to phone/Windows, ~/.awsvault/keys never will), seeding 'aws-vault add' - but Bitwarden should NOT be in the hot path for AWS, since that would trade away aws-vault's short-lived STS sessions for a long-lived key in the environment.

tasks.title: GROUP_FLAGS couples links.sh to install.sh flag names by string
tasks.notes:
Since v0.1.20, links.sh's GROUP_FLAGS names INSTALL_* variables that live in install.sh, resolved indirectly via ${!flag:-}. Renaming a flag in install.sh produces no error anywhere — the group just silently stops linking.

Mitigation in place: tests/test_links.sh asserts every GROUP_FLAGS flag matches a '^FLAG=false$' line in install.sh's initializer block. That works but is mildly brittle to reformatting of that block (e.g. switching to ': ${INSTALL_X:=false}' or one-lining the declarations would break the grep without any real defect).

Worth revisiting only if the initializer block gets reformatted or the assertion produces a false failure. The alternative is accepting the silent-failure class, or moving to a single declaration site — but flags are prompt state owned by install.sh and meaningless to uninstall.sh, which sources the same links.sh.

tasks.title: Restore headless install support via explicit --headless flag
tasks.notes:
v0.1.21 removed $DISPLAY/$WAYLAND_DISPLAY headless detection, so Ghostty and Nerd Fonts are now unconditional prompts — an install on a display-less machine (SSH, container, CI) installs a terminal emulator and fonts nothing can render. Accepted deliberately: no headless targets remain since the move off WSL, and the sniffing was a third encoding of group gating competing with GROUP_FLAGS. Revisit when a real headless target reappears; the fix is an explicit --headless flag or INSTALL_GUI=false, never restored environment sniffing (identity.md and README now state that as policy). Note the suite has no headless path anymore, so this costs a second prompt-stream fixture with its own accepted_categories assertion.

See: output/claude-toolkit/backlog-notes/headless-install-flag.md

tasks.title: Pre-flight hardware check before dual-boot installs
tasks.notes: DUAL-BOOT-TUMBLEWEED.md now has a VMD/RST pre-check (Phase -1), but it was written after losing an evening to it on the Nitro — the guide had no 'inspect the machine before you start' step at all. Worth a short scripted or checklist pre-flight covering the things that silently break an install: storage controller mode (VMD/RST), firmware boot mode, GPU vendor and whether the distro's kernel has a matching driver build, and free space. Script-first applies: this is deterministic inventory, and the same commands ran ad-hoc three times tonight. Blocked on nothing; low priority until a third machine is on the horizon.

tasks.title: setup-toolkit check 8 always flags PROJECT_ROOT as missing
tasks.notes: PROJECT_ROOT is set in the gitignored .claude/settings.local.json because Claude Code passes env values through literally (the template's "$(pwd)" never expands) and a resolved path in the tracked settings.json would be wrong on every other clone. setup-toolkit-diagnose.py's check 8 only reads settings.json, so it reports MISSING_ENV: PROJECT_ROOT on every run. Recurring false positive that trains us to skim check 8. Fix is upstream in claude-toolkit: have the drift check merge settings.local.json env before diffing against the template, or let a project mark an env key as local-only.

tasks.title: Enable treesitter folding for shell and python buffers
tasks.notes: Folding is configured only in after/ftplugin/markdown.lua and json.lua (foldmethod=expr + vim.treesitter.foldexpr, foldlevel=99, foldcolumn=1). In .sh/.py buffers no folds exist, so za/zo/zc silently do nothing. Extend the same per-ftplugin pattern to sh and python, or lift it to a global default with per-ft opt-out. Keep foldlevel=99 (open by default, folding opt-in) -- that is the established convention in both existing ftplugins. Docs: docs/nvim-learning.md currently omits folds because they were markdown/json-only; revisit once this lands.

tasks.title: Document/automate detection of new nvim setup-table mapping sources
tasks.notes: scripts/_nvim_chords.py's NVIM_SETUP_TABLE_HOOK_LUA hardcodes three patch targets (telescope, neo-tree, cmp). A future plugin adding setup-table-based keybinds (vs vim.keymap.set) is invisible to check-keybind-collisions.py's nvim-vs-zellij check until someone manually adds a fourth TARGETS entry -- nothing flags the gap. Low priority: rare event, and the existing three cover this repo's current setup-table plugins.
